matches.quote: The peak assignment of P5 (H(3) or benzoate) should be resolved with the calculated dipolar shifts... Please also explain the "x4" scaling and the line positions at 0.2 T
On the QMC (Fig. 3e), the paper does not state... why Delta J/J = 0.2 was chosen... The QMC is not compared quantitatively with the measured T0 = 0.02J
Fig. 1 is labelled schematic, but its boundaries... are presented as results. Please overlay the measured points and the experimental crossover criteria (T0, the Delta(H) curve).
"The first direct NMR evidence for the coexistence of these two types of excitations" should be toned down, or qualified
The form Kn = a exp(-Delta/kBT) + b is applied to an upturn... so the paper should justify why its temperature scale equals the soliton gap.
The argument that the RS state survives at 0.2 T is qualitative... The low-energy scaling of a random chain in a field differs from the zero-field RS fixed point.
The form Kn = a exp(-Delta/kBT) + b is applied to an upturn... That is an order-parameter-like quantity, not a Boltzmann population, so the paper should justify why
It carries a multiplicative ln^(1/2)(T0/T) correction (Sachdev...)... compare 1/T1f quantitatively with the field-theory prediction including the log correction, using J = 18 K
The robustness of the ILTA decomposition and the error bars on w2 are not shown... show that w2(T) does not change for a range of regularization parameters
The authors should show the linewidth and Kn of a resolved line at 0.2 T (and 0.5 T) against temperature below 0.4 K, and check whether line broadening sets in
give the dipolar tensors computed from the structure (Supplementary Sec. S1)... list the tanTRG Hamiltonian parameters (staggered g, DM vector) and their sources.
Simulate the distribution of local 1/T1 for a weakly random chain at the measured field and temperatures... and compare the simulated P(1/T1), w2(T) and 1/T1s(T) directly with Fig. 3c
show the field dependence of T0 and a. The 0.5 T data in Supplementary Fig. S3 should be analysed like Fig. 3d, with 1 T added if possible.
The link between the ILTA weight w2 and a correlation length, and the claimed log law, are not derived... No argument is given for why the fraction of nuclei
Fig. 3e gives xi/a against T/J without error bars, disorder distribution or system size. Please add these, and state the number of disorder realizations.
The quenched disorder is not identified or characterized... give an independent estimate of the defect concentration and compare it with Delta J/J = 0.2.
Please deposit the raw recovery curves M(t) and the ILTA code and parameters.
Between about 2 K and 100 K, 1/T1 rises by one to two orders of magnitude... The authors should identify this contribution and show it is negligible
The authors should state whether c_s is fitted or taken from the literature, define h, and quote fit uncertainties on Delta at each field.
Fig. 2a shows the lines are not fully resolved at 0.2 T. Overlapping proton sites with very different hyperfine couplings would give exactly a two-component recovery
The paper plots Hhf/H in arbitrary units and compares only the onset temperature (about 0.15J)... compare calculated and measured Kn(T) in absolute units
The peak assignment of P5 (H(3) or benzoate) should be resolved with the calculated dipolar shifts... give the dipolar tensors computed from the structure
The sample temperature and RF heating at 30 to 100 mK are not documented... show that 1/T1 and w2 do not depend on pulse power and repetition time
On the QMC (Fig. 3e), the paper does not state: - how xi is defined (from which correlation function)
The link to the thermal-conductivity downturn below 0.3 K... should be phrased as a hypothesis unless a quantitative estimate (for example kappa from the measured T0 and a) is given.
Overlapping proton sites with very different hyperfine couplings... nuclei relaxing through a channel that becomes visible only once the fast channel saturates
Overlapping proton sites with very different hyperfine couplings would give exactly a two-component recovery with rates two orders of magnitude apart
The authors should show the linewidth and Kn of a resolved line at 0.2 T (and 0.5 T) against temperature below 0.4 K
whether the -ln T range (T/J from about 0.005 to 0.15) is in the asymptotic RS regime or a weak-disorder crossover... cross-check against... stretched-exponential fits
qualified with respect to earlier NMR on disordered and doped spin chains.
cross-check against direct two-exponential (a_s/(a_f + a_s)) and stretched-exponential fits of M(t)
